newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian shares edge up in lazy trading.
newsitem.headline: Russian shares edge up in lazy trading.

text.p: Leading Russian shares edged up on Friday in low volume in quiet pre-holiday trade, dealers said.
The Russian Trading System 23-share index ended higher at 316.89 after Thursday's closing 314.07 on total market volume of $16.71 million.
"We opened with an upwards mood, but buying was only local and prices froze at morning levels," said CentreInvest Securities trader Alexander Pankov.
Most activity was in utility Mosenergo MSNG.RTS and LUKoil LKOH.RTS, where traders said they saw Western selling and local buying.
LUKoil rose to $13.84 from $13.70 at Thursday's close and Mosenergo firmed to $1.37 from $1.36.
"Someone big from the West is selling Mosenergo and LUKoil," a Troika Dialog trader said.
He said Western operators had been selling some leading shares for a second week.
Pankov said he saw Western interest in some shares at good levels, but a shortage of paper, for instance of Nizhnevartovskneftegaz NZGZ.RTS oil company, prevented the market from growing.
"Buyers are not aggressive, that's why everything remains unchanged," he said.
Nizhnevartovskneftegaz was $8.10 on March 5, when it was last traded.
"The market has found a support at these levels," the Troika Dialog trader said.
Pankov forecast a rising market next week, when investors come back from an investment conference in New York.
He said the rumoured appointment of presidential chief-of-staff Anatoly Chubais as First Deputy Prime Minister would encourage foreign investors to buy.
"They will immediately start buying more actively," he said.
UES EESR.RTS rose to $0.2165 from $0.2145, Surgutneftegaz SNGS.RTS oil company edged up to $0.810 from $0.793 and utility Irkutskenergo IRGZ.RTS was $0.266 after $0.267.
